utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Hey Eli, I was just out running errands and heard folks mention the repair drive—what’s the latest?

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: I’ve only heard the basics so far, Ira—seems they’re gathering names and needed fixes before setting a proper schedule. I’d like to see a clear list and times before I commit to anything.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: That makes sense—I’ll keep an ear out while I’m around town and let you know if I hear when they post the list or set times.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Leo, I’m a bit swamped, but tell me the gist—what do you need for the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Mainly spare tools, extension cords, and a couple volunteers for check-in. If you can bring any of that Saturday morning, it’d help.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Got it—I can bring a couple extension cords and maybe help at check-in for the first hour Saturday morning.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Hi Pia, I heard there’s a repair drive happening—can you confirm the details before I start telling anyone else?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I’ve heard about it too, but I don’t want to spread the wrong time or drop-off rules—let me check the notice first before we tell people.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Thanks, Pia—please let me know what the notice says, especially the time and what items they’ll actually accept.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh, the repair drive—yes, I meant to ask what needs fixing first. I can help gather tools, if I remember where I put mine.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Thanks, Oren—first priority is the loose railing by the community steps, then the leaky hose bib near the garden. If you find your toolbox, bring a wrench, pliers, and any spare screws you’ve got.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Right, railing first, then the hose bib—wrench, pliers, and spare screws if I can track them down. I’ll put a note by my door so I don’t wander off with just a sandwich.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Hi Noah, before we get started, can you remind me which repairs we’re prioritizing and who’s already signed up to help?

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh—sorry, Hana, I don’t have the list straight in my head yet. Let me check the signup sheet before I tell you the wrong priorities or helpers.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Thanks, Noah—please check the sheet first, and I’ll wait so we can plan from the right details.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Hey Jules, sorry I’m late jumping in—what still needs doing for the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: No worries, Dane! We still need folks to sort donated items, help with the sign-in table, and spread the word to anyone who might bring a broken appliance or bike.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: I can take the sign-in table for a shift, and I’ll text a few folks who might have bikes or small appliances to bring by.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Hey Gus, I heard you’re organizing the repair drive—what do you need help with?

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Hey Sam, thanks for asking — I could use help setting up tables Saturday morning and sorting the tool bins. If you’ve got a spare extension cord or two, bring those along too.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Absolutely, I can be there Saturday morning to help with tables and tool bins, and I’ll bring a couple extension cords too.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Hi Faye, I’m starting a careful list of where everyone’s repair items are coming from and where they need to go. Do you already have any locations confirmed for the drive?

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: I don’t have anything confirmed yet, but I can check with the school office and a few parents at pickup today. I’ll let you know as soon as I have solid locations.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Thanks, Faye — I’ll mark those as pending for now. Just send me the school office and parent pickup details once they’re confirmed, and I’ll add them to the list.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh Quinn, have you heard when the repair drive is kicking off? I’ve been meaning to tell a few folks, but I don’t want to pass along the wrong time.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: I haven’t heard the confirmed kickoff time yet, Tess, but as soon as I do I’ll spread the word fast. Better we wait than send folks to the wrong place too early.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: That’s sensible, Quinn—I’ll hold off for now and just tell folks we’re waiting on the confirmed time. Give me a holler when you hear, and I’ll help spread it around.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Rey, what exactly needs fixing first, and how many people do we have lined up to help?

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I’m not sure yet, Mina—I’ve only heard bits from a few neighbors. I can ask around today and get you a clearer list of what’s urgent and who can actually help.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Good—please get names, skills, and the top three repairs by tonight so we can stop guessing and make a real plan.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Hey Nell, I heard there’s a repair drive coming up—do you know when and where everyone’s meeting?

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: I’m not totally sure yet—I only heard about it from Marisol. I can ask around and let you know when I get the actual time and place.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Thanks, Nell—once you hear the time and place, let me know and I’ll help spread the word around the block.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Uli, I’m glad we’re getting the repair drive started—do you already have a sense of which items neighbors most need help with?

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: I’m not entirely sure yet, Rosa, but I’ve heard a few folks mention small appliances and leaky fixtures. I can quietly ask around and make a simple list.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That would be wonderful, Uli—thank you. If you jot down the item, the neighbor’s name, and how urgent it feels, I can start matching repairs with volunteers.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh Eli, have you heard the latest about the repair drive? I was just about to ask if you knew what time everyone’s gathering.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: I haven’t heard a firm time yet, Tess. I’d like to pin it down soon so everyone knows exactly when to show up.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: I’ll ask around this afternoon and let you know as soon as I hear a firm time, Eli.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Hey Vik, sorry I’m only catching up now—what’s still needed for the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Hey Dane, I’m still getting the details myself, but I’ll ask around and pass along whatever’s still needed once I hear.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Thanks, Vik—I appreciate it. If you hear they need hands for sorting or hauling, I can jump in later in the day.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Hi Uli, I’ve heard a little about the repair drive, but I’m still trying to understand what’s needed. Is there a way I can help quietly in the background?

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: Yes, quietly would be kind. Maybe you could help sort the small tools or make a list of what’s missing, without much fuss.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I can do that. I’ll start with the small tools and note anything that seems missing without making a stir.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Opal, I’m a bit rushed—what’s the quick version of what you need for the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Quick version: bring any broken small appliances or tools to the community room, and label them with your name, unit, and what’s wrong.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Got it—small broken stuff, labeled with my name, unit, and the issue. I’ll see what I can dig up and drop it by.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Hey Hana, I was thinking the repair drive could be a nice way to bring a few different folks together—do you already have people in mind to help out?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: I like that idea, Jules, but I’d want to check who’s actually available before naming anyone. Are you thinking hands-on repair folks, organizers, or both?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Both, ideally—maybe a couple handy folks for the fixing side and a few organized neighbors to keep drop-offs and sign-ups smooth.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh, hey Mara—sorry, I might be a little behind on the repair drive. What’s the latest you’ve got?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Hey Noah, no worries—we’re still gathering items and volunteers, so you’re not too late. I can catch you up and see where you’d like to plug in.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: That’d be great, thanks—I can probably help Saturday afternoon, if that’s useful. What kinds of items are people bringing in so far?

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Hey Gus, I’m just getting back from errands—have you heard any new updates on the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Hey Ira, I haven’t heard anything new yet, but I’ve got my toolbox ready if they need extra hands or spare tools.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: That’s good to hear, Gus—I’ll keep an ear out while I’m making the rounds and let you know if anyone mentions where help’s needed.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Hey Leo, I’m glad you brought up the repair drive—how can I pitch in?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Thanks, Sam. Could you help sort donated tools on Saturday morning?

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Absolutely, I can help sort the donated tools Saturday morning. What time should I be there?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Before we promise anything, do we know where the repair drive would happen and who’s bringing the tools?

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Good question—do we have the community room available, or are we looking at someone’s garage? And who already has a basic tool kit they can bring?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Let’s check the community room schedule first, because a garage could get crowded fast. I can ask the building office, but we should also make a list of who has tools and what they can actually bring.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Hey Cleo, we’re putting together a repair drive for the neighborhood—want me to send you the details and loop in a few folks nearby?

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Yes, please send me the details, Quinn. I can start a simple supplies list and see what folks nearby might already have to contribute.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Great, I’ll send you the details now and start looping in a few neighbors who might have tools or supplies to spare.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Hi Oren, I’m trying to line up the repair drive around school pickup times—do you know what window people are aiming for?

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh, Faye, I think folks were talking about right after pickup, maybe around 3:30 to 5—but let me double-check so I don’t steer you wrong.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Thanks, that would help a lot—if it’s 3:30 to 5, I can probably swing by after getting the kids settled.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Nell, I’m glad we could connect—I'm starting to pull together the repair drive details, and I’d love to hear what you think the block needs most.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Hi Rosa, thanks for including me—I'm still catching up through what others have mentioned, but I’ve heard a few folks bring up leaky gutters and broken porch steps as big needs.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That’s really helpful, Nell—gutters and porch steps sound like a good starting list. I’ll note those and ask around to see which homes need urgent attention first.
